pins.name: D0
pins.label: D0 (RX)
pins.notes: TFT/SD socket: wired to the onboard Arduino TFT LCD screen socket's RS/DC pin (confirmed via arduino-libraries/TFT source: `TFT EsploraTFT(7, 0, 1);` = CS=D7, RS=D0, RST=D1). Also the standard 32U4 hardware Serial1 RX pin. The TFT screen is an optional plug-in module (socket), not an always-populated onboard chip, so this pin is left available for general use rather than excluded — but a sketch using both hardware Serial1 and a physically-installed TFT screen will conflict (confirmed via a community Esplora pinout write-up: "we are repurposing the display pins ... this will not work well with both something else and a display connected").

pins.name: D1
pins.label: D1 (TX)
pins.notes: TFT/SD socket: wired to the onboard Arduino TFT LCD screen socket's RST pin (confirmed via arduino-libraries/TFT source: `TFT EsploraTFT(7, 0, 1);` = CS=D7, RS=D0, RST=D1). Also the standard 32U4 hardware Serial1 TX pin. Same optional-module reasoning as D0 (see that pin's note) — left available, not excluded.

pins.name: D3
pins.label: D3 (SCL)
pins.notes: TinkerKit OUTPUT connector pin (confirmed via arduino-libraries/Esplora Esplora.cpp source comment: "External outputs: D3, D11") — a direct, non-multiplexed digital/PWM output routed to one of the two TinkerKit OUTPUT connectors on the board, meant for driving the user's own external TinkerKit actuator module. Kept available (same reasoning as a relay output) rather than excluded. Also the standard 32U4 I2C SCL alias, unused for I2C on this board (the Esplora has no exposed I2C header/pins — confirmed via Arduino's own Esplora getting-started guide: "The Esplora doesn't expose pins to provide for I2C communication").

pins.name: D4
pins.label: D4
pins.notes: Accelerometer Z-axis analog input (confirmed via arduino-libraries/Esplora source: `const byte ACCEL_Z_PIN = A6;`, read via analogRead() — a real analog-output accelerometer chip, not I2C). Physically the same pin as A6/digital-id-24 (see that entry) per the 32U4's A6-A11 shared-pin convention (pins_arduino.h PROGMEM port/bitmask tables confirm both digital ids 4 and 24 map to the same PD4 physical port bit). Not general-purpose I/O.

pins.name: D5
pins.label: D5 (Led Red active high)
pins.notes: RGB LED red channel (confirmed via arduino-libraries/Esplora source: `const byte RED_PIN = 5;`, driven via analogWrite()). Active-high inferred from the official Arduino Esplora getting-started guide's RGB fade demo (Esplora.writeBlue(brightness) sweeping 0->255->0 to "see the dimming effect", i.e. higher PWM duty = brighter, no inversion) rather than a schematic transistor/resistor trace.

pins.name: D6
pins.label: D6
pins.notes: Piezo buzzer/speaker driver pin (confirmed via arduino-libraries/Esplora source: `const byte BUZZER_PIN = 6;`, driven via tone()/noTone()). Dedicated onboard actuator (a physical piezo speaker is soldered to this net), not general-purpose digital I/O. Physically the same pin as A7/digital-id-25 (see that entry) per the 32U4's A6-A11 shared-pin convention.

pins.name: D7
pins.label: D7
pins.notes: TFT/SD socket: onboard TFT LCD screen's chip-select (CS) pin (confirmed via arduino-libraries/TFT source: `TFT EsploraTFT(7, 0, 1);`). Optional plug-in module, not an always-populated onboard chip (see D0's note) — left available, not excluded.

pins.name: D8
pins.label: D8
pins.notes: TFT/SD socket: onboard microSD card slot's chip-select (SD_CS) pin (confirmed via arduino-libraries/TFT library's Esplora examples: `#define SD_CS 8`). Optional plug-in module (see D0's note) — left available, not excluded. Physically the same pin as analog channel A8 (digital id 26, see that entry's note) per the 32U4's A6-A11 shared-pin convention.

pins.name: D9
pins.label: D9 (Led Blue active high)
pins.notes: RGB LED blue channel (confirmed via arduino-libraries/Esplora source: `const byte BLUE_PIN = 9;`, driven via analogWrite()). Same active-high reasoning as D5 (red channel)'s note. Physically the same pin as A9/digital-id-27 (see that entry), which is tagged identically rather than excluded, since selecting either identity in the Designer actually drives this LED channel.

pins.name: D10
pins.label: D10 (Led Green active high)
pins.notes: RGB LED green channel (confirmed via arduino-libraries/Esplora source: `const byte GREEN_PIN = 10;`, driven via analogWrite()). Same active-high reasoning as D5 (red channel)'s note. Physically the same pin as A10/digital-id-28 (see that entry), which is tagged identically rather than excluded, since selecting either identity in the Designer actually drives this LED channel.

pins.name: D11
pins.label: D11
pins.notes: TinkerKit OUTPUT connector pin (confirmed via arduino-libraries/Esplora Esplora.cpp source comment: "External outputs: D3, D11") — see D3's note; the other of the two TinkerKit OUTPUT connector pins. Kept available for general use.

pins.name: D12
pins.label: D12
pins.notes: Accelerometer Y-axis analog input (confirmed via arduino-libraries/Esplora source: `const byte ACCEL_Y_PIN = A11;`, read via analogRead() — a real analog-output accelerometer chip, not I2C; this current library source resolves an old, since-fixed discrepancy where a stale comment elsewhere claimed A7). Physically the same pin as A11/digital-id-29 (see that entry) per the 32U4's A6-A11 shared-pin convention. Not general-purpose I/O.

pins.name: D13
pins.label: D13 (Led active high)
pins.notes: Onboard status ('L') LED, active-high — confirmed via community documentation of the Esplora's four onboard LEDs ("L (yellow) connected directly to the microcontroller and accessible through pin 13"), same convention as the standard Leonardo/Uno D13 LED_BUILTIN this board inherits.

pins.name: D14
pins.label: D14 (MISO)
pins.notes: Standard 32U4 hardware SPI bus pin (MISO). Shared (multi-drop) with the onboard TFT/SD socket if a screen module is physically installed (both the TFT and SD card use hardware SPI, confirmed via arduino-libraries/TFT source) — general-purpose SPI otherwise, per the usual multi-drop-SPI keep-available policy.

pins.name: D15
pins.label: D15 (SCK)
pins.notes: Standard 32U4 hardware SPI bus pin (SCK). See D14's note — shared with the optional TFT/SD socket.

pins.name: D16
pins.label: D16 (MOSI)
pins.notes: Standard 32U4 hardware SPI bus pin (MOSI). See D14's note — shared with the optional TFT/SD socket.

pins.name: D17
pins.label: D17 (SS)
pins.notes: Standard 32U4 hardware SPI bus pin (SS). Not used by the TFT/SD socket, which has its own dedicated CS lines on D7/D8 — general-purpose.

pins.name: A0
pins.label: A0
pins.notes: Analog multiplexer address-select line, bit 0 (confirmed via arduino-libraries/Esplora source: `const byte MUX_ADDR_PINS[] = { A0, A1, A2, A3 };`, driven as a digital output to select which sensor channel is read via the shared A4 input — see that entry's note). Not general-purpose I/O.

pins.name: A1
pins.label: A1
pins.notes: Analog multiplexer address-select line, bit 1. See A0/digital-id-18's note for the full explanation of the mux mechanism.

pins.name: A2
pins.label: A2
pins.notes: Analog multiplexer address-select line, bit 2. See A0/digital-id-18's note for the full explanation of the mux mechanism.

pins.name: A3
pins.label: A3
pins.notes: Analog multiplexer address-select line, bit 3. See A0/digital-id-18's note for the full explanation of the mux mechanism.

pins.name: A4
pins.label: A4
pins.notes: Multiplexer common analog input (confirmed via arduino-libraries/Esplora source: `const byte MUX_COM_PIN = A4;`, read via readChannel(), which drives the A0-A3 address lines then either analogRead()s or, only for the joystick button, digitalRead()s this one shared pin) — the SINGLE, time-multiplexed ADC channel for ALL of: face buttons 1-4 (SWITCH_DOWN/LEFT/UP/RIGHT), joystick X, joystick Y, joystick pushbutton, slide potentiometer, light sensor, temperature sensor, microphone, and both TinkerKit analog inputs. None of these have their own dedicated GPIO on this board — each is read by selecting its channel on A0-A3 then reading this pin and, for buttons, comparing against a threshold (>512) or, for the joystick switch specifically, a direct pulled-up digitalRead(). This is a genuine 16-channel analog multiplexer (binary-addressed via 4 digital select lines), not a resistor ladder, but the practical conclusion is the same: none of the buttons/joystick get a simple `button` capability tag, since there is no dedicated per-button digital-input GPIO to tag — tagging this shared analog pin as `button` would be wrong (it is not a digital input at all for most of these channels) and would silently hide the other 11 channels multiplexed through the same physical pin.

pins.name: A5
pins.label: A5
pins.notes: Accelerometer X-axis analog input (confirmed via arduino-libraries/Esplora source: `const byte ACCEL_X_PIN = A5;`, read via analogRead() — a real analog-output accelerometer chip, not I2C). Not general-purpose I/O.

pins.name: A6
pins.label: A6
pins.notes: Accelerometer Z-axis analog input, the A6 analog-channel identity of the same physical pin as D4 (digital id 4) — see that entry's note for the full explanation. Not a separate, independently-usable analog input.

pins.name: A7
pins.label: A7
pins.notes: Piezo buzzer/speaker driver pin, the A7 analog-channel identity of the same physical pin as D6 (digital id 6) — see that entry's note. Not a separate, independently-usable analog input.

pins.name: A8
pins.label: A8
pins.notes: Physically the same pin as D8 (see that entry's note: onboard microSD card socket's SD_CS pin) per the 32U4's A6-A11 shared-pin convention (PIN_A8=26, aliases D8's physical port bit) — not a separate, independently-usable analog input.

pins.name: A9
pins.label: A9 (Led Blue active high)
pins.notes: RGB LED blue channel, the A9 analog-channel identity of the same physical pin as D9 (digital id 9) — see that entry's note. Tagged identically to D9 rather than excluded/left as a plain analog input, since this net is driven by the RGB LED's blue channel, not a free sensor input.

pins.name: A10
pins.label: A10 (Led Green active high)
pins.notes: RGB LED green channel, the A10 analog-channel identity of the same physical pin as D10 (digital id 10) — see that entry's note. Tagged identically to D10 rather than excluded/left as a plain analog input, since this net is driven by the RGB LED's green channel, not a free sensor input.

pins.name: A11
pins.label: A11
pins.notes: Accelerometer Y-axis analog input, the A11 analog-channel identity of the same physical pin as D12 (digital id 12) — see that entry's note. Not a separate, independently-usable analog input.
